given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)

breaks.break: A loan due today counts as overdue (`<=` instead of `<`)
A loan due long before today is missed
'Today' is taken from the local date instead of UTC

given.why: B1 only uses a loan due a day before today (due 03-16, today 03-17). No test in this spec has a loan due exactly today (B2 never creates one), and the clock is fixed at 10:00Z, so a `<=` mistake or a local-date mistake passes.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today

breaks.break: A loan with no reminder at all is skipped
A reminder recorded on an earlier day wrongly blocks today's reminder

given.why: Only the case with no reminder at all is set up. No test records a reminder on an earlier day and expects a new one today.

breaks.break: Open loans are skipped

given.why: Both open overdue loans must be sent, and B2 covers the returned case.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member

breaks.break: Nothing is sent (dry run)
The wrong member id is sent
The wrong loanId or dueOn is sent

then.why: The exact `memberId`, `loanId` and `dueOn` for each loan are asserted, and the count is pinned at 2.

then.part: then records a reminder for today

breaks.break: No reminder is recorded
The recorded date is dueOn or another date, not today
The reminder is recorded for the wrong loan

then.why: The `reminders` rows are asserted exactly: loan ids and `sent_on` 2026-03-17, which differs from dueOn 2026-03-16.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today

breaks.break: A reminder already recorded today is ignored, so the loan is sent again
A reminder from an earlier day is treated as 'today' and suppresses sending

given.why: Running the job twice proves a same-day reminder suppresses a resend. No test has a reminder from a different day, so code that mixes yesterday up with today passes.

breaks.break: Returned loans are still reminded
An open overdue loan is wrongly treated as returned

given.why: loan2 is overdue and returned, and the sent list must be exactly [loan1].

breaks.break: A loan not yet overdue is reminded
A loan due exactly today is reminded (`<=`)

given.why: The test adds copy-3 but never lends it. No loan in the test is un-overdue, so nothing sets this case up.

breaks.break: The returned loan is still sent
The already-reminded loan is sent a second time
A not-yet-overdue loan is sent

then.why: `toMatchObject` on the array pins the length, so the returned and repeated cases are caught. The not-overdue case is never in the data, so sending for it would pass.

given.part: The Notifications API refuses or can't be reached

breaks.break: A refusal is not treated as a failure
An unreachable API is handled differently from a refusal

given.why: The service test uses a refusal. The unreachable case reaches the job as the same `refused` result, and the integration test B5 pins that mapping.

breaks.break: A reminder is recorded despite the refusal

then.why: The `reminders` table must equal exactly the row for loan2.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`

breaks.break: The wrong event name is logged
The wrong level is logged
The loanId field holds another value
The error is a fixed string, not the refusal's reason

then.why: `toContainEqual` asserts the level, event and exact fields, with the reason taken from the fake.

then.part: carries on with the other loans

breaks.break: The job stops at the first failure

then.why: loan1 is refused and is the earlier-due loan, so loan2 is only sent if the job continues past the refusal.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan

breaks.break: The summary is logged before all loans are handled

given.why: The final log entry must carry the counts for all three loans.

breaks.break: The wrong event name is logged
The wrong level is logged
The sent count is wrong
The failed count is wrong

then.why: The last log entry is asserted with `toEqual` on level, event and fields `{ sent: 2, failed: 1 }`.

breaks.break: The client sends nothing when called

given.why: The client is called directly with a reminder and the intercepted request is asserted.

then.part: Sends `POST {NOTIFY_URL}/notifications` with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`

breaks.break: The wrong HTTP method is used
The wrong path is used
The content type is not JSON
A body key is wrong or missing, or the template is wrong

then.why: The full request is asserted with `toEqual`: method, path, content type and body.

breaks.break: Only 200 is accepted
Only 200 and 202 are accepted

then.why: 200, 202 and 204 are each asserted as accepted.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status

breaks.break: Only 5xx answers are refused
The reason does not include the status

then.why: A 400 must give a `refused` result whose reason contains '400'.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable

breaks.break: A network error is thrown instead of returning refused
The reason does not say unreachable

then.why: A connection error is simulated, and the result must be `refused` with a reason containing 'unreachable'.
